elements.element: No obligation on Customer to disclose more favourable third-party commercial offers to Vendor
elements.evidence: "Customer is not required to disclose or match for Vendor any more favourable commercial offer it receives"

elements.element: No obligation on Customer to match/give Vendor the benefit of more favourable offers
elements.evidence: "is not required to disclose or match"

elements.element: No other MFN/most-favoured-customer commitment burdening Customer elsewhere
elements.evidence: §12.3: "Customer has made no exclusivity, non-compete, most-favoured-customer, minimum-volume, or no-hire commitment"

elements.element: MFN (if any) limited to a defined product
elements.evidence: No MFN survives; clause 7.2 now negates the obligation entirely — no product scoping language present
No duration language anywhere in 7.2 or 12.3
No comparison or carve-out language present

reasons: The locked preferred level is fully met: the single operator flip in §7.2 removes both the disclosure and the matching duties that ran against Customer, leaving no MFN obligation burdening us.
§12.3 independently confirms no most-favoured-customer commitment, so the document is now internally consistent.

Fallback elements (defined product, 12-month term, reasonable-comparison carve-outs) are absent, but that is expected and irrelevant because the preferred bargain (no MFN at all) is satisfied; the two levels are not combined.
Minimality holds: only the operative words of the offending sentence were changed; §12.3 and the remainder of §7.2 are untouched, and no new definitions, exceptions, or boilerplate were introduced.
Residual drafting nit (non-material): the retained lead-in "Before engaging another provider" is now vestigial, but it creates no obligation, contradiction, or dangling mechanic.
